headline: This law lets a private foundation build a memorial in Washington, D.C., honoring emergency medical services, using private money instead of federal funds.
what_it_does: It authorizes the National Emergency Medical Services Memorial Foundation to establish a commemorative work on federal land in the District of Columbia and its environs. The foundation alone must collect contributions and pay for the memorial, and no federal funds may be used for its cost. Any extra donated money goes into a National Park Foundation account.
